assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: @TableTest annotation appears on all 5 test methods (shouldAddItemToCart, shouldRemoveItemFromCart, etc.)

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: Five separate @TableTest methods: shouldAddItemToCart, shouldRemoveItemFromCart, shouldApplyCoupon, shouldProcessCheckout, shouldCalculateCartTotal

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: shouldAddItemToCart has 3 rows (empty, new, existing); shouldRemoveItemFromCart has 3 rows; shouldApplyCoupon has 6 rows for validity/replacement; shouldProcessCheckout has 5 rows; shouldCalculateCartTotal has 6 rows

assertions.text: Item operations, coupon application, total calculation, and checkout are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: Separate methods: shouldAddItemToCart/shouldRemoveItemFromCart (items), shouldApplyCoupon (coupons), shouldCalculateCartTotal (total), shouldProcessCheckout (checkout)

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable with its own preconditions
assertions.evidence: Each row specifies full preconditions. Example in shouldAddItemToCart: 'Add to empty cart | [] | widget | 2 | [widget:9.99]' — cart state is explicit, not implied from prior row

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses before/after columns to specify state change
assertions.evidence: shouldApplyCoupon table has 'Active coupon before' and 'Active coupon after?' columns showing state transitions (e.g., 'Replace existing coupon | FLAT5 | SAVE20 | ... | SAVE20')

assertions.text: Coupon application table tests validity and replacement, not type effects on price
assertions.evidence: shouldApplyCoupon tests expired coupon, nonexistent code, and replacement logic. Coupon type effects (percentage vs fixed vs product-specific) are tested in shouldCalculateCartTotal, not here

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: All tables have 'Scenario' as first column: 'Scenario | Cart before | Product ID | Qty | ...' etc.

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?'
assertions.evidence: Multiple output columns end with '?': 'Message?', 'Cart after?', 'Active coupon after?', 'Success?', 'Total?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes
assertions.evidence: Examples: 'Add to empty cart' (condition), 'Replace existing coupon' (condition), 'Expired coupon code' (condition) — not 'Success' or 'Error'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language, not code identifiers
assertions.evidence: Column names: 'Product ID', 'Qty', 'Cart before', 'Cart after?', 'Message?', 'Coupon', 'Total?' — not 'productId', 'quantity', 'result'

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: All test method bodies follow pure arrange-act-assert with single assertion per row. Example: 'CartResult result = ShoppingCart.addItem(...); assertEquals(...); assertEquals(...)'

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest
assertions.evidence: All methods follow order: @DisplayName(...) @Description(...) @TableTest(...). Example: shouldAddItemToCart has @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest in that order

assertions.text: Test method has @DisplayName annotation or clear method name
assertions.evidence: All methods have @DisplayName: 'Add item to cart', 'Remove item from cart', 'Apply coupon to cart', 'Checkout', 'Calculate cart total'

assertions.text: If @Description is present and longer than one line, uses text block (triple-quoted string)
assertions.evidence: @Description annotations use triple-quoted strings: '@Description(""" ... """)' for multi-line text. No string concatenation with +

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method has a single, uniform assertion pattern
assertions.evidence: shouldAddItemToCart: two assertions (message, cart) applied uniformly to all rows. shouldApplyCoupon: two assertions (message, coupon code) applied uniformly to all rows

assertions.text: Product prices, coupon rules, and test data are visible in table or @Description
assertions.evidence: shouldCalculateCartTotal @Description: 'widget=$10.00, gadget=$4.00, hat=$6.00'. shouldApplyCoupon @Description lists SAVE20, FLAT5, PRODW, XPIRED with types and validity

assertions.text: TypeConverter methods convert map/string values into domain objects
assertions.evidence: Four @TypeConverter methods: toCart, toCatalogue, toCoupon, toInventory. Test methods contain only arrange-act-assert (no object construction from raw values)

assertions.text: Coupon data expressed in a single column with @TypeConverter
assertions.evidence: shouldCalculateCartTotal has single 'Coupon' column with @TypeConverter toCoupon parsing formats: '20% cart', '$5.00 cart', '50% widget' (readable shorthand, not separate columns)

assertions.text: Map columns use standard TableTest syntax [k: v, ...] and [:] for empty
assertions.evidence: Cart notation: '[widget:2, gadget:1]', '[widget:2]', '[]'. Inventory: '[widget:10, gadget:5]', '[widget:5]'. Matches standard [k:v] syntax, not custom brackets

assertions.text: @Description does not duplicate information scenario names convey
assertions.evidence: shouldCalculateCartTotal scenarios name coupon types ('Percentage off whole cart', 'Fixed amount off', 'Product-specific discount'). @Description explains calculation rules (sum, minus discount, floored at zero) — not duplicate coupon type names
